name: MisconfigBench taxonomy
description: Controlled root-cause taxonomy for MisconfigBench instances. Case metadata should reference subtype ids instead of duplicating category names.

subtypes.name: Syntax error
subtypes.description: The configuration violates syntax or escaping rules required by the target parser or runtime.

subtypes.name: Invalid option name
subtypes.description: The configuration uses an unsupported, misspelled, deprecated, or wrong-context option name.

subtypes.name: Misplaced configuration
subtypes.description: A valid option is placed in the wrong file, section, block, scope, or precedence layer.

subtypes.name: Duplicate option
subtypes.description: Multiple declarations of the same option conflict or cause an unintended effective value.

subtypes.name: Intra-component error
subtypes.description: A single component's configuration violates constraints among its own options, sections, or runtime assumptions.

subtypes.name: Cross-component error
subtypes.description: Configuration values across components are inconsistent, such as a client and server disagreeing on protocol, address, credential, or mode.

subtypes.name: Resource identifier mismatch
subtypes.description: A configured resource name, path, socket, host, port, database, user, queue, topic, or service identifier does not match the actual resource.

subtypes.name: Resource competition
subtypes.description: A required resource is unavailable because of contention, conflict, exhaustion, or exclusive ownership by another process or component.

subtypes.name: Unauthorized resource access
subtypes.description: The component cannot access a required resource because of permissions, credentials, policy, ownership, ACLs, or authentication constraints.

subtypes.name: Hardware limitation
subtypes.description: The configured behavior exceeds available hardware, kernel, platform, filesystem, memory, CPU, disk, or device capabilities.

subtypes.name: Component incompatibility
subtypes.description: Two or more components are configured in mutually incompatible versions, protocols, feature sets, modes, or assumptions.

subtypes.name: Component missing
subtypes.description: A required dependency, service, plugin, extension, module, binary, certificate, or sidecar is absent from the runtime environment.

subtypes.name: Ambiguous option name
subtypes.description: The option name is valid but misleading, overloaded, or interpreted differently than the operator expected.

subtypes.name: Option value and functional requirement mismatch
subtypes.description: The configured value is valid, but its semantics do not satisfy the intended behavior or operational requirement.
